prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1201; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident and my injury, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. For the record, can you confirm you were the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision in Houston, Texas?
A: Yes, I was driving. It was a head-on thing, but honestly it didn't look like much. We were both going slow, maybe in a parking area turning onto the same road.
Q: Can you describe what happened just before impact?
A: I was turning left and the other car came straight at me. I tried to stop but there wasn't enough room. It was a soft hit, nothing like you see on TV.
Q: Did either airbag deploy?
A: No, I don't think so. The steering wheel didn't hit my chest or anything like that.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I always do.
Q: Can you tell me about your injury?
A: My right shoulder started hurting that same evening. It's sore when I lift anything over my head or reach behind me. I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning and they gave me some pain medication and a sling for a few days.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since then?
A: I've been to my family doctor twice. They want me to do physical therapy, but I haven't scheduled it yet.
Q: Did you have any shoulder problems before this collision?
A: Not that I remember. I played some recreational softball years ago, but nothing recent.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get this resolved so I can get back to normal.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
